market_view: Calm regime (VIX 16.5, down 47% from its 1-year high) with a soft US inflation print, but yields and the dollar stay firm under a hawkish Warsh Fed; the US-Iran conflict is escalating and has driven crude up 12-14% in 5 days.

oil_gas.catalyst: 'Oil prices rise 2% to one-month high as US-Iran attacks deepen supply disruption' (Reuters, 2026-07-14): ongoing Hormuz supply shock, escalating not reversing.
oil_gas.reasoning: Hold XOM from 07-07; the exit condition (de-escalation) is not met and supply disruption is deepening. XOM rose only 2.4% against WTI +12.6% in 5 days, so the move is not fully reflected. Horizon ends about 07-21; Q2 earnings later add variance.

gold_miners.reasoning: Gold bear market (down 15% in 60 days) with firm dollar and near-high 10-year yields; Fed chair signals no tolerance for inflation. NEM headlines are opinion pieces, not catalysts.

chips.reasoning: NVIDIA robotics and Japan partnership posts are routine product news; NVDA already rose 4% on 07-14. Valuation articles are not catalysts. No export-rule or guidance news.

pharma.reasoning: LLY fell 6.7% in 5 days with the whole sector and no stock-specific headline; no trial, approval or pricing news to name. A dip alone is not a catalyst.

copper_uranium.reasoning: 'Cameco Resolves Cigar Lake Disruption' bears on CCJ and uranium, not leader FCX, and removes a supply-shock tailwind. The FCX +3.3% copper bounce is already priced in.

would_change_my_mind: A US-Iran ceasefire or Hormuz reopening would make me exit XOM at once; a named FCX, NVDA or LLY company catalyst (guidance, approval, export change) would make me consider a long.

handoff.what_changed: Iran conflict escalated: Reuters reports US-Iran attacks deepening supply disruption, WTI 79 (+12.6% in 5 days), Brent 85; XOM lagged (+2.4%). Soft US inflation reading and Warsh tells Congress no tolerance for high inflation. Cameco resolved the Cigar Lake disruption.
